name: Unlabeled sample compression
description: Minimum size of an unlabeled sample compression scheme
definition: The **Unlabeled Sample Compression** of $\mathcal{H}$ is the smallest $k$ for which every realizable labeled sample can be reduced to at most $k$ of its instances, without retaining their labels, from which a reconstruction function returns a hypothesis consistent with the whole sample.
graph_summary: Smallest number of unlabeled sample instances sufficient for consistent reconstruction.
origin_references: Kuzmin and Warmuth give an early optimal unlabeled-compression construction for maximum classes in \cite{kuzmin2007unlabeled}. Pálvölgyi and Tardos showed that the optimum can exceed VC dimension, while Chalopin--Chepoi--Moran--Warmuth give a corrected construction for maximum classes; see \cite{palvolgyi2021unlabeled,chalopin2022unlabeled}.

doubly_monotonic.proof: By definition, being monotonic under both subfamilies and projections is doubly monotonic.

c_monotonic.proof: A conditioning is restriction to a subfamily followed by a projection; hence doubly monotonicity implies c-monotonicity.

monotonic.proof: Restricting a compression scheme to a subfamily preserves its size and reconstruction guarantee.

p_monotonic.proof: Projecting a compression scheme and deleting projected-away coordinates preserves its size and reconstruction guarantee.
